notes: Real hardware test of 0.8.0's Sheets logging: the redirect-following fix worked correctly (AT+HTTPHEAD's Location header parsed and followed twice), but the GET of the script.googleusercontent.com redirect target then came back as AT+HTTPACTION reporting '0,200,0' (200 status, DECLARED length 0), immediately followed by an unsolicited '+HTTP_PEER_CLOSED'. cellular.py treated declared length 0 as proof of an empty body and raised without ever trying AT+HTTPREAD at all -- both the Power_Log and GPS_Log POSTs failed this way every time. Root cause: that response uses Transfer-Encoding: chunked (no Content-Length header, since Apps Script output is dynamic), which this modem/firmware reports as declared length 0 via AT+HTTPACTION even though a real body follows; PEER_CLOSED just means the server closed the TCP connection (per SIMCom's manual), not that the response was lost -- the modem still buffers it internally. Fixed: read_http_data() now accepts expected_length=None, requesting a generous 8192-byte cap and relying on the modem's own '+HTTPREAD: 0' terminator (the same marker every prior successful transfer, known-length or not, has always ended with) instead of a byte count known in advance. http_get() (used directly for GET, and reused by http_post_json() when following a redirect) now attempts this read whenever declared length is 0 with a 200 status, instead of raising immediately.
